decisions.text: Two packs, expo and supabase.
The ratchet compares the files the branch changed; no whole-repo count through worktrees.
eslint-plugin-i18next is the expo pack's dependency, installed into the user's repo with consent, never a dependency of cookwright (rule 9).

Plan approved with four P2 amendments (dispositions 21-24) and the answer to the open question (disposition 25); dispositions 3, 4, 5, 7, 11, 17, 18, 19, 20 and the seven-session split accepted as planned.

Rule 3 (claim what was measured): the pack names its rules by what they measure, `strings`, `tokens`, `size`, `design-doc` (expo); `client`, `data-doc`, `types` (supabase); advisory `components-first`, `visual-contract`, `reuse-first`. The kickoff's example `{ "rules": { "max-lines": false } }` used an ESLint rule id; one ESLint id (`no-restricted-syntax`) carries two pack rules and a doc-sync rule has no ESLint id, so the switch is per pack rule: `{ "name": "expo", "rules": { "size": false } }`.

Rule 5 (derived state is never stored) and rule 3: the ratchet lints the base version of each changed file from `git show <base>:<path>` through ESLint's `lintText`, and the HEAD version from `git show HEAD:<path>`, so both sides are commits, never the tree. A blob absent on one side (a file added or deleted on the branch) counts 0 on that side. Nothing is written.

Rule 3: `pack.<name>.count` is not a doctor row. Doctor's budget is 1800 ms and ESLint needs 1.1 s to start (§1); a row that always reads SKIP claims nothing. The repo-wide count is `npx cookwright standards`, printed per rule; the gate runs `npx cookwright standards --ratchet`. The kickoff allowed the SKIP; this removes the row instead, so B-013's "complete" is not defeated by a standing SKIP.

Rule 1 (a harness problem never blocks) and rule 3: a gate check may now say it skipped after it started. `npx cookwright standards --ratchet` exits 11 with one line when it cannot measure, and `runCheck` in `gate.mjs` records exit 11 as `skipped` with that line, the way the hook's `FINDINGS_EXIT = 10` is a convention; `noCheckRan` carries the skip lines, so a fresh app whose only gate check skipped reads why. Any other non-zero exit stays a fail.

Rule 9 (every dependency asked first) and the no-npm rule of init: init never installs `eslint-plugin-i18next`. It reports `skipped  eslint-plugin-i18next  needs npm install --save-dev eslint-plugin-i18next (the strings rule)`, doctor's `pack.expo.lint` WARNs with the same line, and the setup skill runs the install with consent. The strings rule reads SKIP with the install line in the hook until then, never FAIL. The kickoff said "init installs it with consent"; init has no consent surface, the skill does.

Rule 4 (imported, never copied): the ESLint config is `require('cookwright/packs/expo/eslint.cjs')`, spread into the repo's `eslint.config.js`. Init writes that one line when the file is byte-equal to Expo's template (§1), inserting `...require('cookwright/packs/expo/eslint.cjs'),` after `expoConfig,`, with `--dry-run` as the preview; any other file is `skipped` naming the line, and doctor WARNs until the config names the export.

Rule 4 and the kickoff's E-039 path: the pack's two doc-sync rules are config, not logic, so they are written into `cookwright.json` with a pack-owned name (`expo:design-doc`, `supabase:data-doc`): by init into a fresh config, by the setup skill with consent into an existing one. Doctor's `pack.<name>.docs` reads a missing rule as WARN naming it.

Rule 2 (a chosen state is WARN): a rule switched off reads WARN on `pack.<name>.rules` naming it; the sentence stays in the section marked "(switched off)"; no measurement counts it (hook, ratchet, doctor): the engine drops its findings in `countBy` and `wired` does not require it, so a user's own selector on the same ESLint id keeps working; the editor still shows the ESLint rule, which the guide says (disposition 24).

Rule 3: the fixture's scaffold has no ESLint, so a pack measured on it would measure nothing. The fixture installs `eslint`, `eslint-config-expo` and `eslint-plugin-i18next`, each pinned by exact version in `fixture.sh` (disposition 23), and supplies Expo's `eslint.config.js` template from the overlay; `supabase init`'s shape (`supabase/config.toml`, an empty `supabase/migrations/`) comes from the overlay too, since CI has no Supabase CLI. Both are the files a user has after the two commands the getting-started guide names.

Rule 3: the semantic audit is an agent workflow and GitHub CI has no agent, so the kickoff's "calibration run in CI" is split: CI runs the mechanical tiers on the fixture (the `pack.<name>.docs` omission rows at zero, `npx cookwright audit args` producing the two docs with their scopes), and the agent run with an expected zero findings is a QA step on the fixture tree (`KEEP=1`), its result on the closeout line.

Rule 2 and the kickoff's existing-app sentence: `pack.<name>.docs` reads undocumented primitives or migrations as WARN with the count and the first names, never FAIL: a standing omission on an existing app is a count the ratchet makes bearable, not drift the developer caused.
Rule 6 (wanted twice): a `docs-audit` skill ships (E-003, wanted in stage 1 and again here), minimal: branch, `audit args`, the Workflow call, review the diff, the cost line.

Rule 3 (amended by the developer, disposition 21): the size rule measures what the sentence says, functions. `max-lines-per-function` with 150 on `.tsx` and `.jsx` files (a component is a function) and 40 on `.ts` and `.js` files. No `max-lines`: a file limit is a different claim. A directory partition would read a screen outside `app/` as functions (review finding 6).

Rule 1: pack detection is a default, not a gate, and runs on a fresh config only. A fresh config declares `expo` when `package.json` depends on `expo`, `supabase` when `supabase/config.toml` exists or `@supabase/supabase-js` is a dependency; `init --packs <a,b>` overrides on a fresh config and is refused on an existing one like `--hosts`. An existing config never gets a pack from init or migrate (disposition 22).
B-011 rides along (kickoff: "if the plan finds it free"): one more path through `probes.ignored` in `init/gitignore.mjs` and one doctor row, the last checkpoint of s3, dropped first if s3 runs long.

The kickoff's "the setup skill offers to have the agent fill the templates from the code" is kept as an end-pass item of the skill (review finding 5): with consent, on a branch, the agent fills each contract doc from the tree (one entry per listed primitive or migration, one session), then the docs-audit verifies it. The docs-audit has no generate mode and none is built (rule 6: once).

Rule 2 (review finding 8): a hooks setup managed elsewhere (husky, lefthook, a global `core.hooksPath`) is a chosen state, so `hooks.pre-commit` and `hooks.pre-push` read WARN with the reason instead of SKIP, and B-013's "not verified" lists only what could not be measured. A FAIL or a "not verified" the developer cannot clear is a bug by rule 2.

Rule 3 (review finding 1): the fixture asserts `level 0 declared: complete` only when both `gitleaks` and `claude` are on PATH, and otherwise asserts that the `not verified:` list names exactly the absent tools' rows.

Rule 3 (review finding 2): the standards checks never lint a symbolic link. `matching` reads modes (`git diff --cached --raw -z`, `git ls-files -s`, `git diff --raw` for the ratchet) and drops `120000` entries; the exports also carry `ignores: ['.claude/**', '.agents/**', '.codex/**', 'node_modules/**']`.

Rule 3 (review finding 3): the ratchet's base is resolved in order: `--base <ref>`; `COOKWRIGHT_PUSH_BASE`, which the pre-push hook sets to the remote sha of the pushed ref at HEAD when that sha is not the zero sha; when HEAD is on `baseBranch`, its `@{upstream}`; otherwise `merge-base(baseBranch, HEAD)`; none resolvable → exit 11 naming what was tried. A solo developer pushing `main` is therefore ratcheted against what the remote has.
Rule 3: the size rule is `max-lines-per-function` only, 150 on `.tsx`/`.jsx`, 40 on `.ts`/`.js` (disposition 13 as amended).

Rules 2 and 4: existing configs never get a pack. The 2→3 migration writes `packs: []` (outcome `packsAdded`), init never edits an existing config, `--packs` is refused on one, detection runs only on a fresh config. Instead: a doctor row `packs` reads WARN when `packs` is empty and the tree shows a stack (`expo detected (package.json depends on expo), no pack declared; the setup skill offers it`), so an all-PASS readout gives a reason to run the skill (the B-012 lesson); the setup skill's end pass offers the detected packs, written into `packs` with consent, then `init` writes the section, the templates and the pointers, and the skill offers the doc-sync rules and the gate entry (§4.8). The row is PASS listing the declared packs, or `no packs declared, none detected`.

The stage-3 create-expo lesson: the fixture pins `eslint`, `eslint-config-expo` and `eslint-plugin-i18next` by exact version in `fixture.sh`, printed on its first line with the scaffold pins, bumped by hand; the versions are the latest on the day s2 runs.

Rules 4 and 6: no `cookwright.json` reader inside `eslint.cjs` (two readers of one config for an editor-only benefit). The exports are static; switched-off rules are honoured by the engine (disposition 8). The guide says the editor still shows a switched-off rule.
Rule 9, the open question answered: no root devDependency for ESLint. The fake-ESLint seam tests the engine; the fixture is the real-ESLint proof, locally from s2 and in CI on every push.

Findings 0 and 12 (P1, P2), rule 1 and rule 3: the hook pipeline stays synchronous. The pre-commit `standards` check spawns the engine as a child process, `node <bin> standards --staged`, through `spawnSync` with `timeout: 60_000` and `killSignal: SIGKILL`, so the 60 s cap is real and a hung ESLint is one SKIP line, never a hung commit. The check maps the child's exit (0 PASS, 10 FAIL, 11 SKIP, anything else `could not run`) and prints its lines. The engine (`src/lib/packs/standards.mjs`) is async and tested in-process with a Promise-returning fake through `io.loadESLint`; the hook check is tested through an `io.spawn` seam and once end to end through the shim against a fake `eslint` package placed in the scratch repo's `node_modules` (`src/test-fixtures/fake-eslint/`, a Promise-returning `ESLint` class with `version`, `calculateConfigForFile` and `lintText`), so the process boundary is exercised without a dependency (disposition 25 holds).

Finding 1 (P1), rule 5: shared files are transformed once. `rulesFileStep` replaces `blockStep` and composes `AGENTS.md` in one pass from one text: the core block and every declared pack's section, one row per block (`wrote`, `kept`, `updated`), one file write; `eslintConfigStep` inserts every declared pack's line in one transform. A two-pack fresh init and an idempotent rerun are tested, asserting both sections and both lines survive.

Findings 2 and 14 (P1, P2), rule 3: one path base. Every entry the engine handles is normalised to a path relative to the work tree's top; git enumeration runs from the top with the config root as pathspec (`-- <rootRel>/`, or `.` when the root is the top), so a sibling workspace's files are never listed; `git show <ref>:<topRel>` reads blobs; ESLint receives the absolute path (`path.join(top, topRel)`) and runs with `cwd` at the config root; display is root-relative. Engine, hook and ratchet are tested with `cookwright.json` in a subdirectory and an unrelated changed sibling.

Findings 3 and 15 (P1, P2), rule 3: `wired` compares effective options, not presence. From `calculateConfigForFile` it checks severity `error` and, per rule: the tagged message present in the `no-restricted-syntax` and `no-restricted-imports` options, `max` equal to 150 or 40, i18next `mode: 'jsx-only'`. A mismatch reads `overridden by a later block in eslint.config.js` and the rule is skipped on the line (disposition 37), never counted as measured. The Supabase client exemption is `ignores` on the pack's own block (`**/services/supabase.*`, `**/lib/supabase.*`, `**/utils/supabase.*`, `supabase/functions/**`), never a later `off` block that would erase a user's own import restrictions; a test keeps an unrelated user restriction on those files intact.

Finding 4 (P1), rule 3: independently optional measurements are independent gate checks. `freshConfig` writes two entries, `{ name: 'standards', run: 'npx cookwright standards --ratchet', skipExit: 11 }` and, when the `supabase` pack is declared, `{ name: 'standards:types', run: 'npx cookwright standards --types', skipExit: 11 }`; a types skip is its own recorded `skipped` result, which `check.mjs` reads as WARN and the closeout lists. The command never folds one measurement's skip into another's exit.

Finding 11 (P1 plausible, confirmed by the charter's sentence and rule 1): the pre-commit check is a per-file ratchet. For each matching staged entry it lints `HEAD:<path>` and `:<path>` (an added file counts 0 on the HEAD side) and FAILs only when a pack rule's count rises in that file; it prints the findings of the risen rule in that file. Touching a legacy file without adding a violation PASSes; that case is tested and in QA (c). The kickoff's "FAIL names the file, the rule and the line" holds for the rise.

Finding 5 (P2): `SKILLS` in `src/lib/hosts.mjs` gains `'docs-audit': { level: 2, needs: 'workflows' }`; the fixture asserts the `.claude/skills/docs-audit` row; a Codex-only host gets no pointer for it.

Finding 6 (P2), rule 3: the omission listers have exact shapes. Migrations are files matching `^\d{14}_.+\.sql$` directly under `supabase/migrations/`; primitives are `*.tsx`/`*.jsx` files directly under a `code` directory, by basename, plus `<Dir>/index.{tsx,jsx}` by directory name; excluded: `index.*` at the top level, `*.test.*`, `*.stories.*`, `*.styles.*`, `*.types.*`, any `.ts`/`.js` helper, dotfiles (`.gitkeep`). Cases tested: `.gitkeep`, a directory index, a helper file, a duplicate name across a file and a directory.

Finding 7 (P2), rule 3: `audit args` refuses when a declared contract doc is missing, naming `npx cookwright init`; a `--doc` extra must be an existing regular file inside the repo, root-relative, with no symbolic link on its path (`linkOnPath` from `init/files.mjs`), else refused naming it.

Finding 9 (P2): `npx cookwright packs rules` is a command module, `src/packs.mjs`, registered in `cli-main.mjs`: it prints `{ docSync: [...], gate: [...] }` for the declared packs (the doc-sync defaults and the gate entries from the manifests), refuses with one line when no pack is declared, and is tested; the setup skill passes its output through, never retyped.

Finding 13 (P2), rules 1 and 3: the skip exit is opt-in per gate check, `skipExit` in `KNOWN_KEYS.check` and the schema (an integer 1–255), written by `freshConfig` and offered by the setup skill; a check without it that exits 11 is a fail, and that is tested. Outside the gate the command's exit 11 is documented in the standards guide as the gate convention; the doctor and hook paths never see it.

Finding 25 (P3, folded) and finding 4, rule 3: a line names what it measured. When some rules are measured and others are not (the plugin absent, a rule overridden, `types` without its script), the hook's and the ratchet's status covers the measured rules and the line ends with `; strings: skipped, needs npm install --save-dev eslint-plugin-i18next` for each unmeasured rule; the gate's `passLabel` already has this shape. Both lines are tested.
Finding 16 (P2): init's `eslint.config.js` transform (disposition 27) lands in s2 with the overlay, so s4's checkpoint has a wired fixture; the byte test covers both lines.

Finding 8 (P2): `pushContext` returns `{ base }`: the remote sha of the one pushed ref at HEAD when it is not the zero sha; with several refs at HEAD and different remote shas it returns no base and says so in its label, and the ratchet falls through disposition 20's order. `checkGate` passes it into `gateEnv` as `COOKWRIGHT_PUSH_BASE`. Single-ref, new-ref and multi-ref cases are tested.

Finding 18 (P2), rules 2 and 3: the `types` measure accepts exactly one script shape, `supabase gen types <args> > <path>` with nothing after the target (no `&&`, `|`, `;`, second redirect, `npx` prefix); anything else is `skipped, script shape not recognised`. It runs only when `supabase/migrations/**` or the types file changed in `<base>..HEAD`, otherwise `skipped, no migration or types change since <base>`. It reads `supabase migration list --local` first and skips with `local stack behind HEAD's migrations` when the local stack lacks a migration HEAD has; its line says it measured the local stack. A difference with the stack current is `rose`, exit 10, naming `npm run db:types`.

Finding 19 (P3, folded), the secrets rule of `AGENTS.md`: the hook and the command print `path:line:col  <pack rule>` with the pack's own one-line message from `messages.mjs`, never ESLint's message text, which for the strings rule embeds the literal. Tested with a token-shaped literal.

Finding 21 (P3, folded), rule 3: the engine lints with `overrideConfig: [{ languageOptions: { parserOptions: { project: null, projectService: false } } }]`, so a typed-linting config raises no fatal on a path in no project (the base side of a renamed file); the pack's rules need no type information, and a typed rule's own error message carries a non-pack id and is not counted.

Finding 22 (P3, folded): this repo's doc-sync rules are honoured, not escaped: §7.4's specs are `packages/cookwright/packs/**` and `packages/cookwright/src/lib/packs/*`; s6 stages the playbook's Reviewer-role line with `bundle-phase.js` and a first `docs/guides/standards.md` with the setup skill; `src/lib/hosts.mjs` and the fixture's `docs-audit` row are in §5.

Finding 27 (P3, folded): QA (c) hand-wires the two lines into the origin clone's `eslint.config.js` as the setup skill's recipe for `pack.expo.lint` names them; the strings rule's attribute exclude list is measured in s4 against the origin repo's component tree (a throwaway script over its checkout, read-only), so it ships reviewed; QA (b) uses the blank template, or expects `pack.expo.docs` WARN with the count on the tabs template.

Finding 4 (P1), rule 3 and rule 5: a gate check that opts into the convention (`skipExit`) has its first stdout line recorded as the result's `note` on every outcome, not only on a skip, so the state and the landing check carry `expo tokens 3 → 3, size 12 → 12; strings: skipped, needs eslint-plugin-i18next (14 files since <base>)`. `check.mjs` reads a passed check whose note names a skipped rule as WARN naming it, as it reads a skipped check today; the closeout's gate table prints the note. `recordGate` stores `note` for every result (today only skips carry one).

Finding 18 (P2), rules 2 and 3: the `types` precheck compares `supabase migration list --local` with HEAD's migration files in both directions and skips with `local stack differs from HEAD's migrations (<n> ahead, <m> behind)` on any difference, so a migration applied locally for another branch never fails this branch's push.

Finding 21 (P3, folded), rule 3: the engine never nulls the parser's project. Renames are detected (`-M`, status R); a rename's base blob is linted with `filePath` set to the HEAD path, which exists on disk and is in the project, so config matching and typed parsing hold; a deleted file (status D) is not linted and the line says `<n> deleted file(s) not counted`, since a deletion cannot raise a count; a lint that throws (a typed rule without a program, any other rule crash) is caught per file and reads `unmeasured` with the message. Tested with a fake whose `lintText` rejects.

Finding 22 (P3, folded): s5 stages the playbook's "The gate's checks" section with `gate.mjs`, stating the `skipExit` convention and the recorded note, so this repo's `playbook` doc-sync rule is honoured, not escaped.
The fixture's 'already at version 2' assertion stays red until s2 edits fixture.sh, as the plan schedules (§10 s2, the version-3 line); no CI run of the fixture is claimed green before s2 (rule 3).
freshConfig writes packs with detection and --packs in s2, as §10 schedules; detect.mjs is s2's (§4.1 lists it, §10 places it).
§4.9 strings land with the code that prints them, session by session, so no unused string ships (rule 5: derived or dead text rots); s1's reading confirmed.
The three advisory rules belong to the expo pack, the only pack with visual rules; the supabase section has no Advisory heading. Disposition 1 lists them under expo.
docs/guides/updating.md's 'already at version 2' is dated output of 0.1.0 and is s7's guide work; the standards guide's first version is s6's (disposition 43).

39 user-facing strings (migrate outcomes, config validator lines, schema descriptions, section texts, the two manifests' sentences and messages) presented to the developer in chat by the orchestrator after s1; accepted as written pending the developer's ruling at review:model.

eslintConfigStep and packDepsStep landed in s2 as the revised plan schedules (§10 s2, disposition 38); the split's s5 checkpoint 'init's template edit, byte-tested' predates the revision and is met by db036c4, so s5 skips it.
The docs-audit SKILLS entry and the fixture's docs-audit pointer row move to s6 with the skill directory they need (skills.test.mjs requires one per key); disposition 32 holds, its session changes.

Disposition 18's tool-aware level-line assertion lands in s3 with B-013's level line, which it depends on; until then the fixture asserts 'complete' unconditionally, true on this machine and in CI with gitleaks present and claude absent only after s3.

A pack section left in AGENTS.md after its pack is removed from packs is out of this stage's scope: logged as E-040 (rule 6: wanted once), with doctor reading a section of an undeclared pack as WARN proposed as the fix.
init --packs with an empty list is kept as the explicit opt-out of detection on a fresh config and documented in the standards guide (s6/s7); rule 2: a chosen state, named in the config row's note.

Between s2 and s5 a transformed eslint.config.js and the fresh gate checks name pieces that do not ship yet; nothing outside the branch sees them and QA follows review:whole, so no action (rule 3: the fixture asserts only what exists at each session).

s2's user-facing strings (init usage and refusal with --packs, the config row note, the pack section and doc rows, the eslint.config.js rows, the plugin row, the two doc templates' headers) presented to the developer in chat by the orchestrator; accepted as written pending the developer's ruling at review:model.

Disposition 18 amended by measurement (rule 3): the scaffold's CLAUDE.md imports AGENTS.md, so host.rules reads PASS without claude and only gitleaks can make a required fixture row SKIP; the fixture asserts 'complete' with gitleaks on PATH, otherwise exactly 'not verified: tools.gitleaks (see their lines)', and asserts host.rules PASS so a future dependence on claude shows.

Minimal setup-skill rows for packs and repo.node_modules landed in s3 because skills.test.mjs requires every CHECKS key in the skill; the pack.<name>.* recipes are s6's as planned, and until then a pack row that is not PASS ends a walkthrough as 'no recipe', a known gap inside the branch.

Guide prose updated in s3 where the doc-sync rules required it; the dated 0.1.0 output samples stay until s7 re-measures them (rule 5: measured output is never retyped), and getting-started says so beside them.

The packs row reads PASS when any pack is declared, per disposition 22's letter; a tree showing a stack that is not declared beside a declared pack is E-042 (rule 6: wanted once), a candidate for fix:model if review:model raises it.

Disposition 8 reading confirmed: a switched-off doc-sync rule stops the docs row from asking for the rule in hooks.docSync, while the doc's presence and the omission count still measure the contract doc itself (rule 3: those measure the doc, not the rule).
The level line's tails confirmed: after a drift the line keeps '; weak: …' and '; not verified: … (see their lines)', so no measured fact is dropped (rule 3); the plan's truth table named the heads.
